summary: Clarify SDK retry semantics and idempotency when using tool/function-calls across Python, TS, and Go
description: Issue summary: Customer reports uncertainty about how Redwood SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) handle automatic retries when using function/tool-calling features. They want guidance to avoid duplicate side effects and unexpected billing. Impact: Potential duplicate downstream actions (webhooks, DB writes) and higher token usage. Environment: Production us-east for primary app; staging repro available. Steps to reproduce: 1) Use SDK to call chat completion with a function/tool descriptor that triggers an external webhook; 2) Simulate transient network error between Redwood gateway and serving runtime (e.g., drop connection during response stream); 3) SDK observes error and triggers its retry logic; 4) Customer sees repeated webhook calls. Expected behavior: SDK should offer safe retry primitives and guidance for idempotency keys or server-side dedup. Actual behavior: SDK retried request and customer observed duplicate side effects and more tokens billed. Customer asked for per-language code examples and recommended config to make tool calls safe to retry.
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Register a function/tool in the prompt that performs an external POST (webhook) on call.
2. Invoke chat completion with function calling enabled from client (Python/TS/Go) with a stable idempotency-token header set or omitted.
3. Kill the connection mid-stream between gateway and client to force an SDK-level retry condition (network blip / 502 from gateway).
4. Observe that SDK retries the request and the function/tool side effect (webhook) is invoked again.
5. Check billing and token counts; customer reports tokens charged for both attempts.

customer_impact: Duplicate side effects from function calls leading to repeated webhook invocations and unexpected charges. Customer paused a small integration pending guidance.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Maya Patel (Customer): We triggered retries and saw duplicate webhooks. Is there a recommended way to make function calls idempotent across retries?
2026-03-10 - Support (Diego Ruiz): Thanks Maya — we can repro. Can you confirm whether you set an idempotency key in the request headers? Also, which SDK and version?
2026-03-10 - Maya Patel (Customer): Using sdk-python 1.8.0 and sdk-ts 2.1.2 in different services. We didn't set an explicit idempotency header. We expected SDK retry to be safe by default.

2026-03-10 - Support (Diego Ruiz): Default SDK retries are conservative for best-effort responses, but function/tool calling may cause side effects. We're investigating whether the SDK retry logic includes idempotency by default for function calls. Linking ENG. INT-885 assigned to runtime team.

2026-03-11 - ENG (Priyanka Sharma): Investigation started: instrumenting gateway logs and SDK clients. Initial hypothesis: SDK retries on network-level connection errors but doesn't attach idempotency tokens automatically for function calls. Server-side dedupe currently available only for specific write endpoints, not function/tool invocations triggered through function-calling abstraction.

2026-03-11 - Support (Diego Ruiz): Sharing interim mitigation steps and code examples below. Waiting for engineering recommendation about adding optional idempotency-key header injection at SDK call site.
investigation_notes: Reproduced issue in staging: drop connection mid-stream -> SDK retried -> function executed twice.

SDK behavior: python/ts/go clients perform up to 2 automatic retries on idempotent-safe HTTP responses and network errors. However, the SDK classifies a chat completion with function calling as non-idempotent by default (because of potential side effects).
No server-side global dedup was observed for function-calling flows; each request issued to serving-runtime created a distinct request_id and triggered tool execution on successful run.
Edge case: streaming partial responses + retry logic leads to SDK issuing a new full request rather than resuming, so function call occurs again.
Billing: tokens are billed per completed server execution; both attempts billed as completed runs in our metering logs because second attempt completed successfully.

Possible mitigations: 1) Customer-supplied idempotency-key header propagated through gateway to serving-runtime and to tool adapters; 2) Server-side dedupe keyed on (customer_id, model, idempotency_key); 3) SDK opt-in mode: attach auto-generated idempotency keys for function-calling requests when user sets a flag (recommendation).
recommendation_and_workaround: Short-term (immediate mitigation): Set an explicit idempotency token header from the client and ensure the downstream webhook/tool checks for duplicate tokens. Example header: 'Idempotency-Key: <uuid-v4>'.
Short-term (SDK config): Disable automatic client-side retries for calls that trigger external side effects (set retry=0) until a server-side dedupe is implemented.

Medium-term (preferred): Use server-side dedupe — propagate Idempotency-Key through Redwood gateway into runtime and into tool adapters. We'll track engineering work to support optional dedupe for function-calling flows.
Recommended: Add lightweight confirmation step in tool adapter (webhook receiver) that treats repeated payloads with same Idempotency-Key as noop after first success.
code_examples:
Python - explicit idempotency and disabling automatic retries:
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import uuid
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")
headers = { 'Idempotency-Key': str(uuid.uuid4()) }
# disable SDK automatic retry for this call
resp = client.chat.completions.create(model="redwood-chat-1", messages=messages, function_call=... , headers=headers, retry=0)
Server-side suggestion: expose a 'call-status' endpoint where a client can check whether an idempotency-key already completed to avoid re-invoking external side effects.
next_steps: ENG: Add an RFC for optional server-side dedupe for function-calling flows (track in INT-885).
SDK: Add an opt-in flag in all SDKs to auto-generate and attach Idempotency-Key for function-calling requests and document recommended behavior (PR linked).
Support: Share this ticket and short runbook with the customer; provide sample webhook-check code for idempotency.
resolution: Workaround provided and documented. Engineering work scheduled (INT-885) to evaluate server-side dedupe for function-calling flows; SDK follow-up PR planned to add opt-in idempotency header generation and explicit retry controls. Customer accepted workaround and will re-enable integration after testing in staging.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 - Diego Ruiz: Provided customer with short-term mitigation steps and sample code for Python/TS/Go. Confirmed they can test in staging.

2026-03-12 - Maya Patel (Customer): Implemented idempotency header and observed single webhook call on retried scenario in staging. Marking as satisfied for now; will wait for SDK/server fix for production roll-out.
Follow-up: ENG to update SDKs and runtime to support optional dedupe; track in INT-885 (ETA Q2 2026).
